content.Title: Endomyocardial biopsy in patients with suspected myocarditis
content.Indication: Progressive or persistent severe cardiac dysfunction and/or life‑threatening ventricular arrhythmias and/or Mobitz type 2 second‑degree or higher AV block not expected to respond short‑term to usual medical treatment; aim to identify aetiology and indicate specific treatment (e.g., giant cell myocarditis, eosinophilic myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis, systemic inflammatory disorders).
content.Number and sites of the samples: Minimum of 5 but preferably at least 7 samples: 3 for pathology, 2 for infections (DNA, PCR) and 2 for RNA viruses/viral replication. Sample left and/or right ventricle. CMR or PET guided sampling may be considered.
content.Aetiology / Microbial testing: Quantitative PCR viral genome analysis for common cardiotropic viruses (parvovirus B19, HHV4, HHV6, enteroviruses, adenovirus, coxsackievirus) by rtPCR. Viral mRNA for active replication may be assessed (low sensitivity). On indication, search for CMV, HIV, Borrelia, Coxiella burnetii (Q‑fever) and SARS‑CoV‑2.
content.Diagnosis of inflammation: Immunohistochemistry with staining for anti‑CD3, CD4, CD8 or CD45 antibodies for lymphocytes; anti‑CD68 antibodies for macrophages; and anti‑HLA‑DR antibodies.
content.Therapeutic implications: Immunosuppressive therapy may be indicated based on EMB results in giant cell or eosinophilic myocarditis and possibly in sarcoidosis, vasculitis or selected patients with increased cardiac inflammation of unknown origin after multidisciplinary counselling.
content.References / Notes: Guideline mentions use of EMB to identify aetiology and guide therapy; PCR and immunohistochemistry are key diagnostic techniques.
